Population increased in Southend-on-Sea

The estimated population of Southend-on-Sea in 2024 was 185,256 usual residents, a rise of 1.4% since 2023.

This meant that Southend-on-Sea's rate of population change placed it about average among local authority districts in England and Wales.

In the period from mid-2021 to mid-2024, the population estimate of Southend-on-Sea increased by 2.5%.

Over this slightly longer period, Southend-on-Sea was also among the areas that had a broadly average population increase, of local authority districts in England and Wales.

Age profile of Southend-on-Sea

The average (median) age fell to 41.7 years between 2023 and 2024.

You can see how the age profile of Southend-on-Sea has changed since 2011 in the population pyramid below.

sections.content:
Southend-on-Sea is an area that is classed as urban in nature according to the 2021 Census Rural Urban Classification.

By age category, Southend-on-Sea's population of 185,256 usual residents was made up of:

  • 35,189 people aged 0 to 15 years, (19%)
  • 114,258 people aged 16 to 64 years, (61.7%)
  • 35,809 people aged 65 years and over, (19.3%)

    • Compared with England and Wales as a whole, Southend-on-Sea has a slightly lower proportion of people aged 16 to 64 years (61.7% compared with 62.8% for England and Wales).

Contributors to population change

We look at different flows of people into and out of areas and births and deaths to see what is driving population change in each area.

In Southend-on-Sea, the largest contribution to population change in the year to mid-2024 was from net international migration.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Southend-on-Sea
sections.subtitle: How the population changed, by component

sections.content:
We estimate that, for Southend-on-Sea, between 2023 and 2024:

  • More deaths than births led to a fall in the population of 133 people (-0.1%). In total, there were 1,784 births and 1,917 deaths in Southend-on-Sea.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other areas in the UK) increased the population by 572 (0.3%). There were 10,129 people entering the area and 9,557 people leaving the area.
  • Net international migration led to an increase in Southend-on-Sea's population of 2,032 (1.1%) as a result of 2,668 people entering the area and 636 people leaving the area.
  • Other change (which includes changes to armed forces personnel and prisoners) for Southend-on-Sea was less than 0.1%.

Revisions to 2023 population estimates

We regularly revise our initial population estimates as we get more data and methods improve.

Our revised estimate for the population of Southend-on-Sea in mid-2023 is 182,771.

Within this, international migration was revised upwards by 839 people and internal migration estimates were revised downwards by 339 people.

Overall, there was an revision upwards of 500 people.
